target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures define the composition of the 'Investments' line item. D194 (2023) lists debt instruments/equity securities at fair value, AFS/HTM debt securities, and equity method securities. D191 (2024) lists AFS/HTM debt securities and equity securities/debt instruments at fair value or equity method. The subject matter (Investments definition) matches.

D192 (2024) describes a change in presentation where investments are disaggregated into AFS, HTM, and other investments. D194 (2023) defines the existing composition of investments. While related, D192 is about a *change in disaggregation* and *presentation*, whereas D194 is the *definition* of the line item. D192's evidence (P273) discusses the new disaggregation. D194's evidence (P268) defines the components. They are closely related but distinct aspects. However, D192 mentions 'Previously, the disaggregation... was provided in this footnote,' referring back to the content of D194. They are often presented together. Given the high semantic overlap in defining what 'Investments' comprises, they can be considered a matched group describing the Investments line item's structure in each year.

comparisons.peer_topic: Classification and measurement of debt securities
comparisons.peer_summary: Debt securities are reported at trade date and classified based on acquisition purpose: trading securities are at fair value with gains/losses in market making, while other securities are used for ALM and reported as either fair value (available-for-sale or market-making) or held-to-maturity at amortized cost.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Bank of America disclose specific accounting classifications for their debt securities, including available-for-sale (AFS) and held-to-maturity (HTM) categories. Goldman Sachs updated its financial statement presentation in Q4 2024 to disaggregate these specific categories on the balance sheet and in cash flows, whereas Bank of America details the classification logic and measurement basis (fair value vs. amortized cost) for these same categories in its accounting policy notes. While GS focuses on the structural change in reporting presentation, BAC focuses on the operational intent (ALM vs. trading) and measurement attributes that define those same classifications.

sentences.text: Beginning in the fourth quarter of 2024, as the balances have increased during the year, investments are further disaggregated between available-for-sale securities, held-to-maturity securities and other investments in the consolidated balance sheets and the related cash flows are disaggregated in the consolidated statements of cash flows.
Previously, the disaggregation of investments was provided in this footnote.

Substantially all other debt securities purchased are used in the Corporation's asset and liability management (ALM) activities and are reported on the Consolidated Balance Sheet as either debt securities carried at fair value or as held-to-maturity (HTM) debt securities.

Debt securities carried at fair value are either available-for-sale (AFS) securities with unrealized gains and losses net-of-tax included in accumulated OCI or carried at fair value with unrealized gains and losses reported in market making and similar activities.
HTM debt securities are debt securities that management has the intent and ability to hold to maturity and are reported at amortized cost.

comparisons.peer_summary: All of Citi's retained interests in CLOs were classified as held-to-maturity securities as of December 31, 2024 and 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the classification of financial instruments specifically as held-to-maturity (HTM) securities. Goldman Sachs notes that HTM securities are part of the disaggregated investment line items on its balance sheets and cash flows starting in Q4 2024. Citigroup confirms that specific retained interests were classified as held-to-maturity securities as of the end of 2024. Both companies utilize the HTM classification for debt instruments, though GS applies it to a broader portfolio context in its presentation change, while Citi specifies it for particular retained interests.

comparisons.peer_topic: Amortized cost adjustments for credit losses and hedge basis
comparisons.peer_summary: The amortized cost of available-for-sale securities excludes a $49 million allowance for credit losses and $(1.2) billion in portfolio layer fair value hedge basis adjustments at December 31, 2024. Held-to-maturity securities' amortized cost excludes a $103 million allowance for credit losses at the same date.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase explicitly define and report on available-for-sale (AFS) and held-to-maturity (HTM) securities within their investment portfolios. Goldman Sachs highlights the new disaggregation of these categories on the balance sheet and cash flows in 2024. JPMorgan Chase provides detailed metrics for these same categories, noting that the amortized cost for both AFS and HTM securities excludes specific allowances for credit losses and hedge basis adjustments. The core similarity is the reliance on these standard debt security classifications, with JPM providing the granular adjustment data and GS providing the presentation context for the same line items.

comparisons.peer_topic: Disaggregation of India income tax provision
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, India was presented separately for the first time in the components of provision for income taxes, with prior period amounts for Other disaggregated to exclude India.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures describe a change in disaggregation methodology for the current fiscal year (2024) where prior periods were conformed to the new presentation. Goldman Sachs disaggregated 'investments' into AFS, HTM, and other investments for balance sheet and cash flow presentation. Morgan Stanley disaggregated its income tax provision to present India separately from 'Other' for the first time, conforming prior periods to exclude India. Both represent a move toward greater granular disclosure by separating specific components from aggregated categories, though the subject matter (investments vs. tax provision) differs.
